# Make the rail reveal policy a registered, overridable owner

## Context

The [extensibility audit on #18304](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18304#issuecomment-5560546655) identified `RevealStateMachine` as a candidate requiring its own runtime assessment. That assessment now reproduces the missing customization path on merged `8d6c4216ca`: install `Neo.overwrites.Neo.dashboard.dock.interaction.RevealStateMachine.tabClick` before importing Rail, asking it to transition to `revealed`; a real Rail click still returns `revealed-focused`, and the owner namespace is absent.

## The Problem

`interaction/Rail.mjs` constructs an unregistered plain `RevealStateMachine` with `new`. The owner has useful methods and timer injection, but the ordinary Neo application-wide overwrite path cannot reach them. Its JSDoc incorrectly treats runtime-only state as a reason to bypass Neo classes.

## The Architectural Reality

A Rail already owns exactly one machine and destroys it before container teardown. The machine owns pending item, revealed item, transition state and dwell/grace timer. Its output is the existing onChange callback; it has no dock-document write path. This is a per-instance Base owner, not a singleton. The newly landed VesselConversion cut supplies the adjacent construction/lifecycle precedent.

## The Fix

Convert the existing RevealStateMachine module to a registered Base-derived class, with policy defaults and callbacks as configs, transient state per instance, and internal decisions through methods. Replace Rail's raw construction with Neo.create through one overridable creation method; Rail retains teardown ownership. Remove the raw constructor path rather than preserving an alias. Keep the current state transitions, timing defaults, hover opt-in, focus hold and callback shape.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Default/refusal | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RevealStateMachine | Base registration/config/overwrite path | Real Neo.dashboard.dock.interaction.RevealStateMachine identity; independent instances and overridable methods | Existing click/hover policy | Class JSDoc | Pre-import Neo.overwrites through a real Rail |
| Rail creation and teardown | Existing revealMachine lifecycle | One independently replaceable owner per Rail, destroyed with that Rail | Default owner retains current behavior | Rail factory JSDoc | Specialization and two-Rail isolation/cleanup |
| Reveal transitions | Existing state table | Existing snapshots and onChange notifications; no document operations | 150ms dwell, 300ms grace; hover off | Existing state table | Current fake-timer regressions and teardown controls |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The existing module exports a registered Base class; its customization methods/configs use the Neo path and retain per-instance state.
- [ ] A real pre-import Neo.overwrites method changes the outcome of Rail's ordinary input path; a subclass can specialize the owner through Rail's single creation seam without copying its lifecycle.
- [ ] Existing click/hover/dismiss/focus/retarget behavior, explicit timing overrides and change snapshots remain covered. Two Rails own distinct state/timers, and destruction clears only the destroyed owner's pending work.
- [ ] Rail creates and destroys the registered owner; no raw-constructor compatibility path, singleton state, document mutation or renderer rewrite is added.
- [ ] Focused reveal/Rail coverage and the unit suite pass, and generated class hierarchy identifies the owner.

## Out of Scope

Other unregistered dock modules, native windows, Group/history binding, Placement composition, Workspace decomposition, new reveal behavior, broad lint/skills or guides. No changes to merged #18383 or #18392.

## Avoided Traps

Registering a wrapper around the old machine; converting transient state to a singleton; copying transition logic into Rail; treating registration as persistence; treating every unregistered module in the audit as the same defect.

Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR 0029; reveal semantics and document boundary unchanged.
Decision Record: existing ADR 0029 remains authoritative.
